title: PR skill: CodeRabbit review-body nitpicks are never read
description:
What is wrong: the PR skill lists three CodeRabbit channels (status check, issue comment, line-level review comments) and leaves out the pull-request review body, where CodeRabbit puts its "Nitpick comments" and outside-diff comments. Those findings are not threads, so `bot-gate` never sees them, and the skill never tells the author to read them. They go undispositioned and unrecorded.

Evidence at 542f05b:
- skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review/SKILL.md:157-215: the CodeRabbit section names its channels; the review body is not one.
- skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review/SKILL.md:519-530 (§ 6): every finding is re-rated and dispositioned, but the skill never names this channel.
- Seen 2026-11-12: a CodeRabbit nitpick in provisiond-rust PR #6's review body (`w5_accounting.py:94-95`) was never recorded as a follow-up.

Raised by: the severity-policy analysis of 2026-11-12 (nuc report).

Severity: P2. It changes what the procedure does: a whole channel of findings goes unread, so none of them is rated, answered or filed. Not P1: CodeRabbit's review-body items are its lowest tier, the gate deliberately counts only threads, and a missed item loses a follow-up, not a blocking defect. (The analysis proposed P3; it is not P3, because the fix changes what the author does.)

Smallest fix: add a fourth channel to the CodeRabbit section: the review body (`pulls/<N>/reviews`, `coderabbitai[bot]`), with "Nitpick comments" and "Outside diff range" blocks. Say in § 6 that each item there is re-rated and recorded in Follow-ups like a thread, with a reply in the PR conversation since it has no thread to resolve.

Verify: on a PR with a CodeRabbit nitpick block, following the skill lists each nitpick in Follow-ups with a rating; `bot-gate` behaviour is unchanged.

Source: the severity-policy analysis, 2026-11-12, `/var/tmp/severity-policy-manager/analysis/report.md` problem 8.

title: pdf2epub: a drop cap set in one run with its opening quote (`“W`) is not detected
description:
What is wrong: The oversized-letter test needs the run's text to be exactly one letter (`len(letter) != 1`, pdf2epub.py:127), so a `“W` run is never taken as a drop cap. It stays in clustering, and its height merges the lines beside it: `“When the ship … what to expect andthe harbour master was still on duty…`, the same output as c4e21ab.

Evidence at 48fdbd5: lines_of (pdf2epub.py:123-129); a `lines_of()` probe with `“W` (top 298, height 44, left 50, width 50, size 40) beside 17px body lines at tops 300 and 322, left 102.

Raised by: rloop Run skills-1113T0219 Reviewer Panel (Round 1); its follow-up 1.

Severity: P2. P2: a limit of the owner's rule for #119 (a drop cap is a run whose text, stripped of whitespace, is exactly one letter); the output equals c4e21ab and no text is lost.

Smallest fix: Owner decision first; e.g. accept one letter with leading opening punctuation in the same run, and restore the run as one unit.

Verify: Fixture `“W` + `hen the ship…` / `the harbour…` gives `“When the ship…` then `the harbour…` as separate lines.

Source: rloop Run skills-1113T0219 on PR #119 (https://github.com/douglaz/skills/pull/119), pdf-to-kindle-epub skill; the Run exited 2 before its follow-ups were filed.

title: Merge companion: no filing path when the post-merge build fails
description:
The merge companion gives no filing path when the post-merge build fails.

Evidence at b75bc2f: skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review-merge/SKILL.md:211 runs nix build with no failure branch, and :218-220 starts filing only "After the successful post-merge build". If that build fails, nothing says whether or when the PR's Follow-ups get filed.

Raised by: a PR #116 review thread (PRRT_kwDORvrQys62e7n3, on skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review-merge/SKILL.md:219, rated Minor). Rated P2: a real gap in a procedure an agent follows. Not higher: an edge beyond the brief (a merged PR whose base then fails nix build), and nothing is lost, because the list stays in the merged PR's body and can be filed once the base builds.

Smallest fix: say that when the post-merge build fails, the filing step still runs once the base is repaired (or from the merged base commit anyway), and that the report names the pending list.

Verify: read the companion; a failed build leaves a named, reachable filing step.

title: pdf2epub: a list number in the same text run as its item is not treated as a marker
description:

Raised by: independent Claude subagent review rounds on 68259ce.

Severity: P2. P2: the lower-case rejoin rule covers most wraps; only capitalised wraps split.

Smallest fix: Add `\d{1,3}[.)]\s` and letter markers to the fallback; take the hanging indent from the first wrapped line.

Verify: Fixture: `1. Text …` in one run wrapping at a hanging indent to a capitalised word stays one item.

Source: PR #119 (https://github.com/douglaz/skills/pull/119), pdf-to-kindle-epub skill; listed in its Follow-ups.

title: Brief template: no place to record a deferred follow-up filing and its owner
description:
What is wrong: the manager brief template has no place to record a follow-up filing that has been put off. When a lane defers filing past the end of the work (a tracker rule that blocks it, or a PR that keeps the list in its body), the obligation lives only in prose, and a fresh manager at the next phase boundary has nothing that tells it the filing is still owed or who owns it.

Evidence at 542f05b:
- skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:228-236 (Current state): slots for phase, branches, open tickets and decisions; none for owed filings.
- skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:146-151: the exit-2 filing rule, with no record of when it is done.
- Seen 2026-11-12: lean-cyberkrill put filing off until after a merge because of its brief's "exactly 60 identities" tracker rule, and provisiond kept about 15 follow-ups only in PR #6's body and the briefs. Neither was tracked as an owned to-do.

Raised by: the severity-policy analysis of 2026-11-12 (nuc report).

Severity: P2. A gap that can drop follow-ups at a manager handoff. Not P1: no requirement is made false, and the filing rules themselves are right.

Smallest fix: add a Current state bullet to the template, `<follow-ups owed: what, where they will be filed, when, and who files them>`, and one line in SKILL.md telling the assistant to carry that bullet into each new manager's brief until the filing lands.

Verify: read the template; a brief for a lane with a deferred filing has the item, its trigger and its owner in Current state, and a fresh manager reading only that brief knows the filing is owed.

Source: the severity-policy analysis, 2026-11-12, `/var/tmp/severity-policy-manager/analysis/report.md` problem 7.

title: pdf2epub: an opening quote kerned into a drop cap sends the letter to line 2
description:
What is wrong: A separate `“` run overlapping the letter by more than the 2px slack makes line 1 fail coverage, and the cap attaches to line 2 (`“hen the ship…` / `Wthe harbour…`), contrary to the docstring.

Evidence at af919d8: covered() (pdf2epub.py:146-160 at af919d8); Run report items 9–10 and the post-Run /code-review.

Raised by: rloop first-line/space Run Reviewer Panel.

Severity: P2. P2: needs a quote kerned over 2px into the cap.

Smallest fix: Ignore punctuation-only runs when testing coverage, and reject rather than move down.

Verify: Fixture quote at left 72 width 12, cap at 80, gives `“When…`.

Source: PR #119 (https://github.com/douglaz/skills/pull/119), pdf-to-kindle-epub skill; listed in its Follow-ups.

comments.author: master
comments.text: Second trigger of this defect, from rloop Run skills-1113T0219 follow-up 7, re-checked at 48fdbd5: line 1's own run starts more than 2px inside the cap's right edge. It fails the neighbour window (`r[2] >= left + width - 2`, pdf2epub.py:134), so the walk starts at line 2. A `W` at top 298, height 51, left 50, width 40, with line 1/line 2 lefts 87/89 or 85/90, gives `hen the ship…` then `Wthe harbour…`; with a cap at top 300, height 40, whose upper half does not reach line 2, the cap is not detected and the lines merge. Ignoring punctuation-only runs would not fix this trigger. The first-line/space Run's report item 9 named it too ("A line-1 run starting 4px inside the box behaves the same way") and suggested tying the 2px slack to the body em.

title: pdf2epub: a drop cap more than one body em from its text is not detected
description:
What is wrong: The adjacency bound (`runs[j][2] - (left + width) > reference`, pdf2epub.py:170, added in 08dc532) rejects a cap whose first line starts more than one body em (the page's dominant font size) to its right. The letter then stays in clustering and its height merges the lines. With `W` (top 298, height 44, left 50, width 40, size 40) and 17px lines at left 106, 108 or 112 (gaps of 16–22px, body 15), the output is `When the ship … expect andthe harbour master…`, as at c4e21ab. At left 104 (gap 14) it reads correctly.

Evidence at 48fdbd5: lines_of (pdf2epub.py:168-171); `lines_of()` probe.

Raised by: rloop Run skills-1113T0219 Reviewer Panel (Round 1); its follow-up 2. At that Run's tree the window was one body height; master's bound is one em, so the fallback starts at a smaller gap.

Severity: P2. P2: a gap over one em is wide for a drop cap; the bound is deliberate (08dc532: do not borrow lowercase text from a distant column); the output equals c4e21ab.

Smallest fix: Owner decision on the bound; e.g. keep a rejected oversized letter out of clustering so its height cannot merge the lines beside it.

Verify: Fixture with a 20px gap gives `When the ship…` then `the harbour…`, and the distant-column guard stays green.

Source: rloop Run skills-1113T0219 on PR #119 (https://github.com/douglaz/skills/pull/119), pdf-to-kindle-epub skill; the Run exited 2 before its follow-ups were filed.

title: pdf2epub.test: the one-em adjacency guard cannot detect the rule failing to fire
description:
What is wrong: `GUARD one-em gap opens an ordinary paragraph` checks only `

When the`, which still holds when the rule does not fire. Evidence at 08dc532: pdf2epub.test:882-883 at 08dc532. Evidence at e9c15f9: the guard is now pdf2epub.test:1062-1063 (`em_body == 12 and '

When the' in em_doc`). It still holds when the rule does not fire. With the bound mutated to `>=` (pdf2epub.py:170), with the lowercase rule disabled (pdf2epub.py:173-174), and with c4e21ab's script, the fixture gives `

`. The check can still fail, and three mutants turn it red: - the cap is left unflattened, keeping its 40pt size in the line, which gives `

W hen the ship…

`; - the cap is restored after the line's runs; - a space is always added after the cap. title: Severity texts: no step tests a P2 against each P1 clause before it is listed
description:
What is wrong: the severity texts list the P1 clauses, but nothing tells a rater to test a finding against them before calling it P2. Raters weigh a finding as a whole, call it "not blocking", and list it at P2 while one of the P1 clauses applies. A rater who writes "could be argued P1" is not told to settle it by clause, so it stays P2.

Evidence at 48fdbd5:
- skills/multi-reviewer-loop/references/disposition-rules.md:11-26: re-rate on the rubric; lowering a P0/P1 needs file:line and raising names the clause. No step tests a P2 against the P1 clauses.
- The Reviewer scale has no such step either: skills/multi-reviewer-loop/references/reviewer-panel.md:302-312 and :857-867, skills/second-model-bead-audit/references/reviewer-panel.md:126-136, skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review/SKILL.md:322-332. The re-rate steps at skills/second-model-bead-audit/SKILL.md:224-229, skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review/SKILL.md:519-523 and skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:153-156 only point at the rubric.
- Filed or listed at P2/P3 on 2026-11-12/13, then re-rated P1 by clause when their owners checked the analysis's flags on 2026-11-13 (owner-accepted, or merged in the owning tracker):
  - `pvr-7tx` (provisiond): a requirement made false; OPS-13 and OPS-27 identifiers are wiped at reconciliation (reconciliation.rs:603-604). Its own auditor had written "could be argued P1 (OPS-13 made false)", and it stayed P2 with no clause decision;
  - `pvr-ggy`: the money clause, LDG-32 made false; debits post against a deleted machine and the hold sticks (business.rs:480-525, deletion.rs:228);
  - `dsp-uz2` (desktop): the money clause; a time-locked XMR deposit is dropped with no refund path (daemon.rs:1055-1056, 1387);
  - 16 of 20 igc sanitizer leaks: raised to P1 `review-preexisting` under the money, secret or data-loss clause, because identity data reaches a committed fixture (instagram-collector tracker PR #48, e04d98e);
  - two checks that could not fail: igc `ziup` (the mention scan cut to 30 characters and all 60 tests still pass) and `8bye` (an assertion raises in a server thread, where it is swallowed).
- Checking matters as much as flagging: of the analysis's under-rating flags checked so far, 21 were confirmed P1 and 8 were kept at P2/P3 with evidence. A flag is a candidate until someone tests it by clause.

Raised by: the second severity-policy analysis of 2026-11-13 (nuc report, laptop and desktop summaries); the re-ratings above by the owning sessions.

Severity: P2. Findings the policy's own clauses put at P1 are listed as follow-ups, so a P1 that should hold the change can be accepted. Not P1: the clauses themselves are right, and a rater who applies each one gets the right answer; the gap is a missing step, and every case above was still recorded and filed.

Owner's ruling to respect (2026-11-13, on `dsp-wn8`, Monero transaction private keys written to logs): "Keys in the logs I see as P2". The clause test must not move such a key in a log to P1. Record the ruling beside the secret clause with its case, and do not widen it: whether it covers other credentials in logs (an API key in a readable log, say) is the owner's call, not the rubric writer's.

Smallest fix: in disposition-rules.md § Classification, one step: "Before rating a finding P2, test it against each P1 clause by name: wrong behaviour in a supported case; a requirement of the brief not met; a test or gate that cannot fail; a requirement made false or contradictory; core function broken; reachable money loss or misdirection; a reachable secret exposure (the owner's 2026-11-13 ruling rates a Monero transaction private key in a log P2); data loss or corruption. If one applies, it is P1. A finding someone calls 'arguably P1' is decided by naming the clause it meets, or the evidence that it meets none." Add one line to each Reviewer scale copy ("test a P2 against each P1 clause before tagging it") and point the three re-rate steps at the new step.

Verify: read the rubric and each scale copy; each tells the rater to test a P2 against the P1 clauses by name and to settle an "arguably P1" by clause. Re-rating `pvr-7tx` and `ziup` with the new text names a clause for each; re-rating `dsp-wn8` keeps it P2; an API key in a readable log is not exempted by the text.

Related: `skl-q11` (age never lowers a rating), a different defect. Same gap in rloop-spec's `PRM-2` and `PRM-4`, filed there.

Source: the second severity-policy analysis, 2026-11-13, `/var/tmp/severity-policy-manager/analysis/report2.md` check 4 and problem 1; `analysis/laptop-summary2.md`; `analysis/desk-dsp-sources.md`; owner pick "Beads + tell sessions" ("The judge and any hand-built review must test every P2 against the P1 clauses").

title: pdf2epub: a one-letter chapter numeral beside a lowercase title is taken for a drop cap and the heading is lost
description:
What is wrong: The lowercase rule takes any oversized single letter whose first covered line starts in lowercase within one em, including a chapter numeral such as `V`, `I` or `X`. The chapter heading is then lost. At 48fdbd5, with `V` (138pt, top 60, height 100, left 50, width 60): - on a chapter page with body text, after a body page, a body-size title `tristeza não é depressão, e como saber a diferença` at top 70, left 120, above `CAPÍTULO` at top 120 gives `

Vtristeza não é depressão, e como saber a diferença CAPÍTULO

`; - on a one-page document with body text, the same layout with a 13pt title `the second chapter and its surprising consequences` gives `

CAPÍTULO

` and `

Vthe second chapter…

`; - on a one-page document set entirely in 24pt type (title at top 62, `CAPÍTULO` at top 120) it gives `

Vthe second chapter… CAPÍTULO

`. c4e21ab gave `

CAPÍTULO V — …

` for all three; the change came in dc8e10a. Capitalised and all-capitals titles keep c4e21ab's heading. Evidence at 48fdbd5: lines_of lowercase test (pdf2epub.py:172-174); probes through parse, classify and build_html. Raised by: rloop Run skills-1113T0219 Reviewer Panel (Rounds 2–3); its follow-ups 9, 13 and 14. Under that Run's size rule (discarded) they also hit capitalised titles; on master only lowercase titles are affected. Severity: P2. P2: checked against the P1 clauses. The owner's rule for #119 ("a big single letter is a drop cap only when the next text continues in lowercase") makes this layout a drop cap by decision, so it is a limit of the decided rule, like skl-kul. It needs a chapter title that starts in lowercase, and no text is lost. Smallest fix: Owner decision first; e.g. do not take a letter as a drop cap when an upper-case label word sits among its covered lines. Verify: The three layouts give `

CAPÍTULO V — …

title: Brief template: a post-Run diff read and a brief's scope cut are not rated by clause
description:
What is wrong: the brief template treats rating as something a review does, so two steps that also decide a defect's severity are not named as ratings. A manager who reads a finished Run's diff and finds a defect files it at a severity it picked on its own, and a brief writer who puts a known defect out of a Run's scope sends it out unrated; the Run hands it back unrated and the caller files it at whatever priority it is told. Neither bead says who rated it or how.

Evidence at 48fdbd5:
- skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:117-118: the Task section says "what is out of scope", with no rule for a known defect put there.
- skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:153-166: "For the review after a Run, re-rate every finding" covers Reviewer findings; it does not say that a defect the manager finds itself while reading the diff is a finding of that review, rated by clause, nor that a scope cut is a rating.
- skills/multi-reviewer-loop/references/disposition-rules.md:209-212: a filed item names "the Reviewers that raised it", with no slot for who rated it outside a Reviewer panel.
- Seen 2026-11-12 on the desktop (dsp):
  - `dsp-uz2` (time-locked XMR cannot be refunded through the API): a manager read the diff of Run dsp-1112T2050 after it ended and rated it P2 itself. No review skill was loaded; the Run's report does not mention a refund path. On 2026-11-13 it was re-rated P1 under the money clause (a time-locked deposit is dropped with no refund path, daemon.rs:1055-1056, 1387), and the owner accepted that.
  - `dsp-2ys` (API keys stored in plaintext): a manager writing the Run brief put "storing only a hash of each key" out of scope (task.md:90-91); the Run handed it back unrated (finished.md:87); it was filed P2 on the session's instruction. Nobody rated it.
  - Both managers had the severity text in context.

Raised by: the second severity-policy analysis of 2026-11-13 (desktop summary and its dsp-source note).

Severity: P2. Two paths put a defect into the tracker with no rating against the rubric, so a P1 can be filed as a follow-up (as `dsp-uz2` was) and a defect the change introduced can be cut from scope instead of being sent back. Not P1: both cases were still filed, so nothing was lost, and `dsp-uz2` has since been re-rated; this bead claims no rating for `dsp-2ys`, which is for the dsp session.

Smallest fix: in the template's Run instructions,
- a known defect left out of a Task section is rated by clause before the instruction goes out; one the change introduces or that leaves the Task unmet at P0/P1 is not cut without an owner pick; the rest go in the instruction as follow-ups with their rating;
- in the post-Run review paragraph, a defect found by reading the Run's diff is a finding of that review and is rated by clause the same way;
- every filed bead says who rated it and in which step (judge, post-Run review, scope cut, owner pick).

Verify: read the template; a scope cut and a post-Run diff read each end in a rating by clause; a bead filed from either names its rater and step.

Related: `skl-uab` (the post-Run paragraph restates the filing rules), a different defect on the same lines.

title: PR skill: beads a pre-PR review loop wrote ride in the source PR
description:
What is wrong: the skills give two filing times for the same follow-ups and never say which wins when a review loop runs before a PR. `multi-reviewer-loop` files its FILE findings at its own finish into the working tree and leaves the tracker write uncommitted. `pr-with-codex-bot-review` then lists follow-ups in the PR body and files them only after the merge, on a metadata PR, at the merged base. Nothing tells the PR author to keep the loop's tracker write out of the source branch, so the beads get committed with the change, before the merge and without the "still holds at the merged base" check.

Evidence at 542f05b:
- skills/multi-reviewer-loop/SKILL.md:994: "At the finish, file each finding dispositioned FILE ... Leave the tracker write uncommitted, as the loop leaves everything."
- skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review/SKILL.md:432-437: P2/P3 and older P0/P1 go in the PR body's Follow-ups; nothing about tracker writes already in the tree.
- skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review/SKILL.md:528-530 and skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review-merge/SKILL.md:214-238: filing happens after the merge, on a fresh metadata branch from the merged base.
- Seen 2026-11-12: 11 follow-up beads were committed on their source PRs before the merge (bitcoin-consulting #40; instagram-collector #18, #23, #25, #26, #27). Only instagram-collector #21 to #22 and skills #116 to #117 used the post-merge metadata PR.

title: Brief template: the post-Run review does not flag listed P2/P3 sites a Run repaired
description:
What is wrong: the post-Run review checks a Run's commits for P0/P1 defects but not for P2/P3 repairs. The template forbids repairing a P2/P3 in the change "even beside P0/P1 repairs", yet nothing tells the reviewer to compare the Run's diff with the follow-ups the Run listed, so a listed P2/P3 site that a P1 repair also rewrote goes unnoticed and is either filed as if it still held or dropped silently.

Evidence at 48fdbd5:
- skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:135-139: review the commits against the Task section; "never repair P2/P3 in this change, even beside P0/P1 repairs". No step checks the diff against the listed follow-ups.
- skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:146-151 and :153-166: follow-ups a later repair removed are listed "as resolved, not filed", with no flag saying the change repaired a P2/P3.
- Seen on the desktop, 2026-11-12/13: 11 P2/P3 were fixed, fully or partly, as side effects of P1 repairs in rloop Runs, 4 of them accepted up front in the judge's brief (T0654 task-2.md:80-82). Nothing in the outer review flagged them.

Raised by: the second severity-policy analysis of 2026-11-13 (desktop summary).

Severity: P2. The owner's rule that P2/P3 are never fixed in the same change goes unenforced after a Run, and P2 repairs add review surface the policy was written to avoid. Not P1: the rule is stated correctly; this is a missing check, and the repairs found so far caused no P0/P1.

Smallest fix: one bullet in "When the Run ends `done`": for each follow-up the Run listed, check whether the Run's diff touched its file:line; name each one it repaired in the report as "P2/P3 fixed inside the change", with the commit, so the owner sees it. Do not revert it on your own.

Verify: read the template; a post-Run review of a Run whose P1 repair also rewrote a listed P2 site names that P2 in its report.

Related: the same check for the Run's judge, filed in rloop-spec; the outer manager's own widening of the change, filed separately here.

Source: the second severity-policy analysis, 2026-11-13, `/var/tmp/severity-policy-manager/analysis/desk-summary.md` check 3; owner pick "Beads + tell sessions" ("P2 fixes slipped into P1 repairs are flagged").

title: Severity texts: say that predating the change never lowers a rating
description:
What is wrong: the severity texts say an older P0/P1 outside the brief is filed at "its own" priority with `review-preexisting`, but none says outright that predating the change never lowers a rating. Raters read "pre-existing" as a reason to rate P2, so P0/P1 defects are filed as `review-followup` and `review-preexisting` goes unused.

Evidence at 542f05b:
- skills/multi-reviewer-loop/references/disposition-rules.md:11-14 (lowering needs file:line), :40-43 (older P0/P1 are FILE) and :218 ("0 or 1, its own").
- skills/pr-with-codex-bot-review/SKILL.md:528-530 and skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:153-160 restate the same, also without the rule.
- Seen 2026-11-12: `igc-p1m` (Run igc-p09), a bearer token sent to a non-loopback listen address, lowered from P1 to P2 as pre-existing, though any reachable secret exposure is at least P1. The provisiond PR #6 post-Run audit rated two API exits "P2 preexisting" (`src/api/funding.rs:133`, `src/api/mod.rs:1177`), though a crash of core function is a P0 clause. No bead in the window carries `review-preexisting`.

Raised by: the severity-policy analysis of 2026-11-12 (nuc and laptop reports).

Severity: P2. A missing statement that let P0/P1 defects be filed as P2; they are still filed, so nothing is lost, but they get the wrong priority and label. Not P1: "its own" priority already implies the rule, so following the text carefully gives the right result.

Smallest fix: one sentence in disposition-rules.md § Classification: "Age never lowers a rating: a P0/P1 that predates the change stays P0/P1. If it leaves the brief unmet it is sent back like any other; if it is outside the brief it is FILE at its own priority with `review-preexisting`." Point the PR skill's § 6 bullet and the brief template's post-Run paragraph at it. Keep the existing scope rule (disposition-rules.md:28-30) unchanged: an older P0/P1 that leaves the brief unmet still sends work back.

Verify: read the three texts; each tells a rater that an old P1 stays P1, is filed with `review-preexisting` only when it is outside the brief, and is sent back when it leaves the brief unmet; no text allows "pre-existing" as the reason for a lower rating.

Merged into this bead: the analysis's proposal to add "a process or watcher exit is a crash of core function" to the rubric. The two API exits were rated low because they predate the change, not because the crash clause was misread, and the rubric already names "a crash or corruption of core function" as P0 (disposition-rules.md:16-17). The proposal's other half, "P3 requires no behaviour change", is already the P3 definition (disposition-rules.md:23-24).

Source: the severity-policy analysis, 2026-11-12, `/var/tmp/severity-policy-manager/analysis/report.md` problem 3 and the laptop summary's top problem 4.

title: Brief template: no instruction for a Run that exits 1 with P0/P1s open
description:
What is wrong: the brief template's Run instructions say what the outer manager does when a Run ends `done` and when it exits 2, but not when it exits 1 (blocked). A Run that blocks with P0/P1 defects open has no instruction, so the outer manager can accept the work and file those P1s as P2 follow-ups.

Evidence at 542f05b:
- skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:135-151: a `done` Run and an exit-2 Run are covered; exit 1 is not.
- skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:106: only the Drain lane stops on "rloop exits 1 or 2".
- skills/delegate-to-manager/references/manager-brief-template.md:153-155: lowering a P0/P1 needs a one-line reason with file:line evidence.
- Seen 2026-11-12 (lean, Run lf-wp5b, about 11:00Z): the Run blocked with 7 P1 rows. The outer manager accepted it at a "review-ratchet stop", closed the task, and filed the rest as `kernel-okf` at P2 `review-followup` on "no current exposure", with no file:line for the lowering.

Raised by: the severity-policy analysis of 2026-11-12 (laptop report).

Severity: P2. A gap that let open P1s be accepted. Not P1: the existing lowering rule (:153-155) already forbids what happened, so following the text as written still gives the right result; the gap is that exit 1 has no path of its own.

Smallest fix: add to Run instructions: when a Run exits 1, leave the task open. A P0/P1 it reports that the Run introduced or that leaves the Task section unmet is sent back through another Run or taken to the owner, and is filed lower only with the file:line reason that :153-155 requires. An older P0/P1 outside the Task is filed at its own priority with `review-preexisting`, as :138 already says.

Verify: read Run instructions for each exit (0 done, 1 blocked, 2 failure); each says what happens to the task and its open P0/P1s.

Not filed with it: fixing a filed P2/P3 in the same change after a Run (`igc-x5z`, `igc-m3v`, `kernel-sot`), which manager-brief-template.md:138-139 already forbids.

Source: the severity-policy analysis, 2026-11-12, `/var/tmp/severity-policy-manager/analysis/laptop-summary.md` (P1 answer, top problems 1 and 2).

Raised by: the second severity-policy analysis of 2026-11-13 (nuc report).

The analysis proposed P3; it is not P3, because the fix changes the procedure. Not P1: CodeRabbit does not gate (ADR 0004), and the codex gate still covers every file.

Smallest fix: add the warning as a third case under the status check: grep CodeRabbit's issue comments for "Review coverage is incomplete"; when present, name the files from its review info, say the review is partial in the report, and re-trigger or read those files before calling CodeRabbit clean. `bot-gate` may print it like the skipped-files list, without gating on it.

Verify: on PR #51, following the skill reports CodeRabbit's review as partial and names the 4 files; `bot-gate`'s exit codes are unchanged.

Related: `skl-01f` (CodeRabbit's review-body nitpicks are never read), a different channel and defect.
